"O.L.: Do you remember them having documents that they had been released from the prison? "S.B.: I don't even remember of asking documents from them. Well, I -- I -- as I said, I don't even think about asking their documents. As -- it didn't come across my mind that during an offensive, after this, documents will be issued. So I couldn't figure that out at all. "O.L.: Okay. From who -- where did you get the confirmation that these people actually had been released? Did someone give you this information? "S.B.: Well, I came -- I realised it based on what was among -- what was discussed among the civilian population because I was afraid myself -- yes, I was afraid myself because I didn't get any official confirmation that they were released and so I was afraid of making any -- not the right thing. So I let them go further with no official confirmation. "A.W.: You said when you were trying to confirm you tried to call on the phone. Where did you try to call on the phone? "S.B.: Yeah, I'd like to get in touch with Klecka -- I tried to get in touch with Klecka, sorry. "A.W.: But you weren't able to get in touch with Klecka? "S.B.: As I touched earlier this subject, I was -- there was no -- there was nobody who was very eager to talk to me at that time because of the problems that I was experiencing. So everyone was trying to avoid or trying to run away from me. "A.W.: Okay. You said that later on you were able to inquire and find out that you had done the right thing to let them go? "S.B.: Yes. "A.W.: And who was it who told you that? "S.B.: Jakup Krasniqi confirmed this. He told me that you've done the right thing. Yeah, he thought -- Jakup Krasniqi thought first there was a provocation on my side. So I asked their opinion being in the main headquarters place when bigger suspicion were being circulated around me. This helped -- this helped force -- this helped add further this information, rumour around me. "A.W.: And did you ever speak with Celiku about this? "S.B.: Yes, I've talked to him. Being in my position, I was the one who had to clarify this, to sort out these issues with everybody. Well, even Celiku himself. I don't know whether he had these second thoughts or not, his reserves about my -- my action, but nobody of them in principle told me or told me openly that you didn't do the right thing. "A.W.: When did you talk to Celiku about it? "S.B.: This happened later. After with -- after the population had taken -- had taken shelter into these gorges. As it was -- as the offensive was going on. And then there was a total chaos during the offensive so we weren't able to talk with each other. "A.W.: Do you think it was in days or in weeks? "S.B.: Yeah -- so it was rather a matter of days. Three, four, or five days later. "A.W.: And where -- did you talk to him face to face or on the telephone? "S.B.: Yeah, face to face. "A.W.: And where did you have the conversation? "S.B.: With -- I don't know whether -- where about the place I talked with him about this case, but what I know is I've seen him and I've met him in Luzhnice, I've met him in Klecka as well. "A.W.: Okay. "S.B.: It might have happened -- it might have happened that we talked with each other about the case on the way from Luzhnice to Klecke being in a Jeep. "A.W.: And what did he say about it? "S.B.: Very briefly but very to the point, concise. It's okay, it's okay. No, he said, it's all right. There's nothing wrong. That's all he said. "A.W.: And you told him that you had seen these people on the tractor and that they had come from Lapusnik and that allowed them to continue? "S.B.: Yeah, of course. I had to clarify the matter as I was the one put in a difficult position. So I explained to him that I decided to set them free, let them go further. I said, Have I done anything wrong? He said, No, that's okay."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at 5 to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, before the witness comes in, we would draw your attention to the fact that the witness has been giving evidence since mid-morning of last Thursday and under leave to cross-examine since late on Monday. And the process is extremely drawn out and the value that might be obtained from this witness must inevitably be limited from what has transpired, so that we would ask you give serious attention to the time that has been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour. I do expect to finish today. I would say that the Prosecution expects to make a similar motion with respect to this witness's prior interview that was made with regard to another witness. And for that reason, I think it's important to give this witness an opportunity to comment, even though it's drawn out, to comment on various passages in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say we had anticipated the application, but bear in mind my observations about weight in any context, given what has occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Powles pointed out to me some of what Your Honour has been saying has been missed off the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have I been edited out of mercy or some other --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You've been shortened and some of the good bits have been left out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be, I'm sure, picked up when the tape is played at the end of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hasten to say it's not remotely critical. It's just an observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski, your concern for my well-being --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm not frighten of criticising Your Honour, it's the shorthand reporter I'm afraid of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the witness, please. That gives you about 55 minutes to run, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, after hearing that passage of the transcript, do you remember now that the tractor with the prisoner -- with the men on it, that the men said that they were in fact from a prison in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as we could see it here it's the 26th and 27th of July where -- when I was not in Kroimire village, and you know the reasons why I couldn't be in Kroimire due to the problems that I had and due to the fightings that I took part in Blinaje and Zborce. I could stop a tractor under a certain suspicion only on the 23rd and 24th of July. Otherwise, on the 25th and 26th July there is no way that I could possibly be in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I just want to ask you about this event that you describe here in the passage that we played before the break. Do you remember this tractor of men that you -- you remember them telling you that you were from the Lapusnik prison, regardless of the exact date?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that because I was told that they came from Lapusnik and the way -- how they interpreted it why they were in Lapusnik -- it is another issue. Simply, as a prison I never concepted [as interpreted] it and I told you as well that there's no way that there was a prison in Lapusnik or a camp there. But it's a different story how civilians interpreted it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I'm going to ask you another question. Did you -- you then tried to make contact with Klecka when you saw this tractor of men. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tractor that I stopped on the 23rd or 24th of July, I stopped it because there were men on board, there was civilians, and they intended to go in the direction of the villages in the plain and that's why I stopped that tractor. And of course I wasn't in position to decide what to do with this tractors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you tried to get in touch with Klecka. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I tried to establish contacts with Klecka in order to see what to do, what the -- with the civilian tractors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later you had a conversation with Fatmir Limaj about this tractor from Lapusnik. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had conversation with many people regarding these issues because I thought that I was I wasn't doing the right thing when I allowed the tractors to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could focus on Fatmir Limaj. You had a conversation with Fatmir Limaj. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had not only one conversation but many conversations with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told -- you told him about the tractor and he told you that you had done the right thing. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I discussed the issue of the tractors that I allowed to proceed in that direction and I always had this conviction that I did not do the right thing. And for this issue, I discussed it not only with Fatmir Limaj but with many others, especially with Jakup Krasniqi because I suspected that I might have allowed them to proceed in direction of the occupying forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Fatmir Limaj told you you had done the right thing. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fatmir Limaj told me that, You did the right thing with the tractor because after their -- them insisting, it was necessary to allow them to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move into my next group of questions - my last group of questions - I'd ask that the Court caution the witness under Rule 90(E), please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I've been asked to remind you of something you may well know already. It's done out of caution so that you're aware of your rights. If any question is asked of you which you think might tend to incriminate you, you may object that you do not wish to answer that question. If you feel that some question is one that might incriminate you, it's open to you to object that you don't want to answer it for that question. That's just so that you're aware of that as you are asked questions by counsel. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move into evidence the witness's prior OTP interview of the 28th of April, 2003, the English version, the Albanian version, and the videotape of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received, but you will understand that gives no indication of where any application might lead us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand that perfectly well, Your Honour, and -- I would, however, at this time move that the Court treat the prior interviews as substantive evidence and consider them for the truth of the matters stated therein for the reasons that are set forth in the Prosecution's motion of 14 February 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your motion is noted. It will be considered along with the similar motion in respect of another witness in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution 160, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just to be clear, all three -- the two transcripts and the videotape are -- have one number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, 40 minutes early and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Commended, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield, is it fair to look at you at this stage of the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Certainly to look, but whether it goes much further I'm not sure. May I ask for a moment to address Your Honours perhaps in fairness in the absence of the witness in relation to observations that you made a little earlier after the break. It will only take me a few minutes but it may shorten matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, counsel wish to put some further matters so us. Could we ask you, please, to wait outside the courtroom. It's suggested it won't take long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, the matter in a sense of having for some assistance in relation to where we go from here with regard to this witness. Plainly there are a number of questions, substantial questions, I would want to ask this witness. But in the light of the indication given after the break about the value of this witness, then it may be unnecessary. I certainly don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I don't think any of us on this side would wish to take up any more time if in fact even on a temporary basis --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me. I just wonder if we should be in private session for this discussion about the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, with the concurrence of Mr. Mansfield, yes; otherwise you mightn't have induced me, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mansfield. Cross-examined by Mr. Mansfield:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, good afternoon. I represent Fatmir Limaj and I'm sorry also you have been here some time and I do have a few questions which I'm afraid I can't complete tonight but I should complete tomorrow. I want to make clear that I'm going to concentrate --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm just trying to -- I'm not getting any sound on my earphones. Maybe now. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to concentrate on the circumstances surrounding the interview you've been taken through, and I'm not going to do any more of that tonight, you've been taken through in April of 2003 with the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to -- if you wouldn't mind thinking back to the situation in 2003. What was the first you heard about the Office of the Prosecutor wanting to speak to you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a summons from the Office of the Prosecutor pursuant to Article 2 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence for an interview, and before I was interviewed the investigator from the Milosevic case, whose name was Barney, wanted to meet me to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm just checking but is the second name or the surname of the investigator from the Milosevic case who wanted to meet you, is his name Kelly?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you informed that he wanted to speak -- or meet with you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called me by phone and through the interpreter he invited me to meet him in his office in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to his office in Pristina and meet him?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was present in the office in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was him and the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a record being kept of this interview in Pristina or meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, records were not being taken during this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was said at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barney Kelly explained to me that that meeting was organised upon the request of investigator Ole Lehtinen, whose name I didn't know at that time. He wanted to meet me and to interview me. So Kelly suggested that I should accept this request for interview and to tell what I know about this case. He explained to me that the procedure of the interview would be the same as the one that we followed in Milosevic case. I requested that only in the case that such procedures were being followed, I would of course cooperate with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what did you understand you were being asked to speak about in relation to this case?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll put it more simply. Why did you think -- we'll come to what was actually said. Why did you think that anyone wanted to speak to you about this case from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought - in case I can now express my opinion - that the reason I was meeting them was because Prosecution has suspicion that I might not want to meet them. Barney Kelly knew well my interest in giving that statement in Milosevic case and he told me that I should be interviewed by the investigators for my activities in 1998/1999 and that I should cooperate with the Prosecution just to avoid any possible misunderstandings of me not wanting to cooperate with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this meeting with Mr. Kelly, did he indicate to you that you might be suspected of anything by the Prosecutor? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not discuss this issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think that you were suspected by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The impression of many KLA soldiers is that all KLA soldiers are looked from an angle of suspicion, and of course everyone, especially senior figures, were suspicious that there was investigations that in fact did not happen but that were rumours that were spread in the population. My impression was that it could be also an investigation on -- of my own acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was the meeting, just roughly speaking? Are we talking about 10, 15 minutes? Half an hour, or what?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it took longer. About an hour, an hour and 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long before the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that took place on the 28th of April, 2003, was this meeting with Mr. Kelly?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four or five days before my interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the interview on the 28th of April, before the recording began was anything said to you by Ole Lehtinen about the Kelly meeting that you'd had?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, it was said that the purpose of the meeting with Barney Kelly was to avoid any misunderstandings regarding the interest that the Prosecution had in my activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Lehtinen indicate to you what the interest was that they had in you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The written summons I received to report to the Finnish KFOR division in Lipjan, premises, was -- had three questions or issues, that is my activity in 1998/1999, the functions I had during the war, and third -- I don't remember the third topic. They were more or less the main topics of their interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Ole Lehtinen before the tape-recording began indicate to you that what you'd been told by Mr. Kelly about the procedure to be adopted, that that procedure would be the same as the one in the Milosevic case. Did Mr. Lehtinen say anything along those lines?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not, but I think that he said that I assume you have clarified this issue with Barn Kelly and he started the actual interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to go back in time a little bit. Before April of 2003 but after the war itself in Kosovo, through 1999 to 2003, were you yourself arrested at any time during those years, 2000, 2001, 2002, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my departure from the Kosovo Protection Corps, I was treated to a very painful way. My -- I was surveyed wherever I went. My place of residence was photographed, my car. And in 2000 I was arrested by the KFOR troops or, to put it better, I was detained for ten days. And after nine days of isolation, the judge who was an Albanian came to me to read the indictment which consisted of two lines. Apart from my name and last name it was written that I was charged for illegal possession of weapons which constituted a criminal offence. And then he started laughing, telling me that if I had a revolver -- a pistol without permission then I would be accused of a criminal offence, too. After my release I was again surveyed and every movement I made was recorded. Life in Kosova for me and many other people like me has become a true hell. People are being arrested like Ganu Ymeri [phoen] or another person from Prizren whose name is Ruzhdi Saramati or Semi Veseli, people who are arrested and then released after two or three years being declared innocent. So all this pressure was brought to bear against me even though no indictment was made against me and no charges were made against me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any truth in the allegation being made against you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained, the charge was for criminal offence, which means a serious offence, for arms possession -- for legal [as interpreted] arms possession. I had a weapon which I had a permission for, and that was a charge made against me by the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the time of this detention in the year 2000, were you still a zone commander or had that ended in the TMK?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had just left TMK on my own wish and I had joined the political and civil life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the period between that detention in 2000 and the interview in 2003, had you been detained on any other occasion in that period?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detained, yes, in the sense that I was constantly surveyed and spied on, in a way. They had the car -- they had a picture of every car that I used and they followed every movements that I made, checked on my house from outside, but that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 2001, you were approached by the Prosecutor in the Milosevic case in order to provide material for that case, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean in -- with regard to the procedures followed then, the procedures for the interview --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll come to that if I may in a moment. I just want to identify so you're clear. I'm talking about 2001 when you were approached by the Prosecutor about Milosevic. So that's the period. All right? Now, I have available the Albanian version to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I wonder if Your Honour would permit him to have the Albanian version of this statement in front of him. I think Your Honour has the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This is a witness statement which was finalised in October of that year, and I want to go through some of the dates. It's finally signed off on the 4th of October, 2001, so it's that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Buja, would you look at the first sheet, first page, of this statement which indicates the dates of the interviews in 2001 and the places for that matter. If you just follow it for the moment. You were interviewed on the 25th of August, 2001, the 20th, the 25th, and 29th of September, 2001, all of those interviews in Pristina; and then another one on the 2th of October, 2001, at Recak. Do you see that? It should be on the front page.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just on the question of date, if you turn right to the end of this statement you'll see what we have as a witness acknowledgment and also an interpreter's certification both dated the 4th of October, 2001. Do you see those at the end of this statement? You'll have to go through the statement and you'll find page 26 and 27, it's the last two pages of the statement, in the English version. I think it's the same in the Albanian. Witness acknowledgment dated 4th of October; interpreter's certification dated the 4th of October. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, the question I have in relation to this is on the occasions you were interviewed before the statement was finally signed off on the 4th of October, were the interviews tape recorded so far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not tape recorded, but notes or taken on the basis of my answers. I don't know of any tape-recording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So was the procedure that the -- the interviewer, Barney Kelly, who you met just before the April interview in 2003, took notes as you spoke over those occasions in August and September and that sometime after the last interview in September a statement was compiled in which what you had said in the interviews was reduced into the statement? Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a procedure followed. These meetings lasted -- those notes were being taken and interpretation was sometimes wrong or it was misinterpreted. That's why often it was necessary for me to intervene when I saw that they were mistakenly translated. So they made corrections. And at the next meeting I looked over those corrections and this is how it went. I improved the mistakes or I corrected the mistakes three times, even after I came here as a witness against -- I mean in the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the occasions before the statement was compiled at the end, are you saying that you were in a position to have the notes taken by the interviewer read back to you in Albanian so that you could then correct what had been written down in the interview? Have I got that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, because always the statement was translated to me. I made the necessary remarks or changes in some parts of the statement that was not correctly translated by the interpreter. And this is why the procedure lasted longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when it came to the statement itself, we can see - but you can confirm - that on each page of the 27 pages you have signed each page yourself and dated it the 4th of October. Do you see that? Each page is signed by you. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it here in the copy that I have, but I was told and -- that I should sign each and every one of the pages of my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what appears to have happened with the statement, if you just bear with me, is according to your acknowledgment which is on page 26 of the English version, may I just read it. You will find it in Albanian. I think it's the second-to-last page, page 26, should be. I just pause to make sure you have to second-to-last page. Do you have that with "witness acknowledge" at the top?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the numbers of the pages here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, right. Well, will you bear -- because it's late I'm not going to ask you to try and find it. I'm just going to read to you what you signed in relation to this. And if you just listen carefully this is what it says: "This statement consisting of 27 pages has been read over to me in the Albanian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection. I have given this statement voluntarily and I am aware that it may be used in criminal proceedings before the International Criminal Tribunal for the prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of international law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia since 1991 and that I may be called to give evidence in public before the Tribunal." Now, is that an accurate description of what had happened, namely that the 27 pages had been read over to you in Albanian and that you'd then signed them?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entire statement was read over to me in Albanian and then I signed every page of that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just on this topic continuing, were you given a copy of the statement to take away with you, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember to have been given any copy, but I could have access to this statement every time I wanted. This happened when I came in The Hague to testify. I was -- I read this statement for three days and I made two corrections of mistakes that occurred during the interview or during the compiling of this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you a slightly more difficult question. In this statement, in the substance of this statement, you do deal with the organisation and the structure of the KLA. Do you remember being asked about that during interviews, and that it -- there is reference to it in the statement? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of this statement now? Do you have a copy of this statement -- I know you have it in front of you. Sorry, what I mean is do you have possession of a copy of this statement since the time that Ole Lehtinen gave you a copy, it would appear, of this statement?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a copy of that statement. I didn't think I needed one, but after what happened with Ole Lehtinen I demanded that if they really wanted me to cooperate with them then they should provide me with a statement I made for the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the recording. Everything, the transcript and the other transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come to the other transcript because what I want to -- probably overnight if you have a copy because you've been given one before. The question is this: Can -- are you in a position to help as to whether the statement describes everything you said about the structure of the KLA or did you tell them more which they didn't bother to reduce into the statement? Now, do you follow the question first of all?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the question. I have always tried to explain the part dealing with organisation -- my part in the organisation of the KLA and I have always made the necessary corrections and improvements. They asked me to make a brief description of my activity and my engagement in that structure and then to pass on to the question of testimony for the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in 2001 when you were doing this, did Barney Kelly at any stage ask you about Fatmir Limaj or Celiku in any detail?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't ask me in any details, but he asked me about my contacts with other soldiers and I gave him the answers that have been included in the statement regarding the organisation of the KLA. It was a brief history or description of the flow of events having to do with my engagement in the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. Would that be a convenient moment? Could I ask the witness if he would refresh his memory from the Albanian version of this statement so I can ask him a few more questions tomorrow on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we will adjourn tonight and resume at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
